title: Knowledge Center (/home/svcacct/AI/DB) is genuinely safe for concurrent multi-user writes
symptoms: Direct user question: does /home/svcacct/AI/DB have real multi-user concurrency safety, or could concurrent users corrupt each other's writes
root_cause: N/A -- this is a verified architecture property, not a bug.
fix: N/A -- no fix needed. Verified by reading tools/knowledge_center/broker.py's real code (not relying on memory/assumption): a real cross-process _ShardLock using fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX), scoped per (category, protocol) shard via a locks/<category>__<protocol>.lock file (different shards never block each other; the same shard is fully serialized across every concurrent user/process), with the full read-index -> write-record -> update-index critical section inside the lock. Writes use _atomic_write_json() (tempfile + os.replace(), an atomic POSIX rename) so a reader can never observe a torn/partial write. This holds only because every write goes through the one server-side broker.py process (invoked per-call via the relay) -- never a network-mounted directory written to directly by multiple machines.

verification.regression: N/A -- pre-existing code, verified by direct source inspection this session

note: Explicit contrast for future reference: dv_harness/memory.py and dv_harness/blackboard.py (the per-project .dv-harness/ runtime state -- state.json, blackboard/, react/, events.jsonl) have NO such locking -- plain read-modify-write, safe for one process, a silent lost-update race for two. This is why the multi-user usage pattern (USAGE_MULTI_USER_SAFETY.md) treats the Knowledge Center and a project's own --project-root runtime state completely oppositely: share the former freely, never share the latter.
